$description: Canonical typography source. Hand-edit this file only; dist/ is generated.

meta.note: The six size steps coincide exactly with Tailwind's own defaults (xs/sm/base/lg/2xl/3xl). The reference skips Tailwind's xl (20px) entirely. That means a Tailwind project gets this scale for free; the other stacks need it written out.

sans.usage: Everything that is not code or a tabular figure.

mono.usage: Code, identifiers, environment keys, and figures in tables or usage meters. Used at one size only (12px) across the whole reference.

declaredUnused.Archivo: Declared in the Paper file's font list but used on zero nodes. Not a token. Either leftover, or a display face that was never applied — worth confirming before anyone adds it.

scale.$note: Size steps only. Semantic styles below are what application code should reference.

display.usage: The one big figure on a card: a balance, a goal total. Carries tabular numerals.

heading.usage: Largest card title. One per card at most.

title.usage: Stat values and prominent section titles (3.4 kW, May 25 2024). Drop to weight 500 with letterSpacing -0.45px for centred empty-state titles, which is how the reference sets them.

body.usage: Introductory and supporting copy under a title.

text.usage: The default. Table cells, list rows, descriptions, most interface text.

prose.usage: Long-form paragraphs that run several lines. NOTE the fractional line height: the reference sets 162.5%, which lands on 22.75px at 14px. Round to 23px, or normalise to 24px for a 4px grid.

label.usage: Form field labels and switch titles. NOTE the fractional line height: 137.5% lands on 19.25px. Round to 19px, or use 20px to match text.

button.usage: All button and tab labels, at every button height.

caption.usage: Help text, timestamps, chart axis labels.

eyebrow.usage: Small uppercase label above a title (RETIREMENT, UPCOMING, COVER ART).

code.usage: Identifiers and keys: env var names, token names.

code-value.usage: The value beside a code key, set in muted-foreground.

numeric.usage: Figures in usage meters and dense tables, where digits must align in a column.
